## Zechariah 13 — Verse-by-Verse Commentary Notes

---

### v. 1: "On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity."

- **Connection to chapter 12.** The phrase "on that day" ties this verse directly to the great mourning of Zechariah 12:10–14. The fountain is opened only after Israel sees the One they pierced and repents. The cleansing flows from their embrace of the Messiah (Guzik, Enduring Word). Eugene Merrill likewise notes that the lamentation of repentance "will in turn result in their forgiveness" — the positive side of genuine conversion is restoration to fellowship, while the negative side (removal of idols and false prophets) follows in vv. 2–6 (Precept Austin, quoting Merrill).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/zechariah-13-commentary

- **The "fountain" is the blood of Christ.** John Gill identifies the fountain expressly with Christ's blood, noting the link to Zechariah 12:10 ("the One they have pierced"). From His pierced side flowed blood and water — blood for justification and remission, water for sanctification. The fountain is "opened" because its virtue is continual; it is never sealed but always stands open (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Inexhaustible provision.** Charles Spurgeon (Baptist) stresses that it is a fountain, "not a cistern nor a reservoir." A fountain continually bubbles up and is as full after fifty years as at the first. God's mercy for forgiveness "continually flows and overflows." Spurgeon also emphasizes that it is *open* — "not a fountain hid and concealed, and closed and barred and bolted" (Spurgeon, "The Open Fountain").
  - https://www.spurgeon.org/sermons/the-open-fountain

- **"Sin and impurity" cover both guilt and defilement.** The Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (JFB) commentary states these two terms refer to "judicial guilt and moral impurity," implying that both justification and sanctification flow from the blood of Christ, not from ceremonial sacrifices (JFB).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **The fountain is figurative, not literal washing.** Precept Austin notes that "no amount of external washing cleanses sin and impurity in our heart," explicitly countering any teaching that water baptism is necessary for cleansing (Precept Austin).
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/zechariah-13-commentary

- **Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges** notes the form of the promise is "Jewish, the substance Christian." The lustral waters of the Law (Numbers 8:7; 19:9) were contained and renewed in a bowl or laver; here they are replaced by a "living fountain of the Gospel, opened once but remaining open ever" (Cambridge).
  - https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/zechariah/13.htm

- **Charles Feinberg** (conservative Jewish-background scholar, quoted at Precept Austin) writes that the fountain "was opened long ago at Calvary potentially, now actually for them. Israel now enters into the provision of God at Calvary." He sees this as both justification and sanctification: "Judicial guilt and moral impurity will be removed at the same time" (Precept Austin quoting Feinberg).
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/zechariah-13-commentary

- **For all ranks and classes.** The "house of David" (royalty) and "inhabitants of Jerusalem" (common people) represent the whole nation. Gill adds that mystically these refer to "all the family of Christ the son of David, and … the whole church of the firstborn" (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 2: "And on that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will erase the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land."

- **God cuts off the sources of uncleanness.** David Guzik observes that idolatry and false prophecy were the two main ways Israel was led astray. God not only provides a fountain to cleanse but also promises to eliminate the sources of defilement (Enduring Word).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Not merely the idols but their very memory.** JFB states that God will "cut off the names" — to destroy their authority, power, and influence so thoroughly that they are "no more remembered" (JFB).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **The "unclean spirit."** JFB identifies this as a "spirit of uncleanness" (cf. Revelation 16:13), opposed to the "Spirit of holiness" (Romans 1:4) — one assuming to be divinely inspired but actually in league with Satan. Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary calls these "seducing spirits" linked to false prophecy (1 Timothy 4:1–3; Revelation 16:13).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html

- **Gill applies this to the end of the Roman Catholic system.** He sees the "idols" as images of the Virgin Mary and saints worshipped by "Papists," quoting Revelation 9:20. The "false prophet" refers to the entire papal hierarchy — pope, cardinals, bishops, priests — and the "unclean spirit" to the spirits of devils that come from the mouth of the dragon, beast, and false prophet (Gill). This is a distinctively Protestant historicist reading.
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 3: "And if anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, ‘You shall not remain alive, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the LORD.’ When he prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will pierce him through."

- **Zeal for God overrides natural affection.** Even parents — who would normally protect their child — will enforce the death penalty prescribed in Deuteronomy 13:6–10 and 18:20 for false prophets. "Love to God shall then have priority over parental or natural family ties" (Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary). Guzik says this shows a coming day when public opinion will be so committed to the Lord and His truth that even false prophets' own families will condemn them.
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Gill** likens the false prophets to the followers of the "man of sin" who "speak lies in hypocrisy" (1 Timothy 4:1). When their imposture is fully exposed, even their parents will not spare them (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 4: "And on that day every prophet who prophesies will be ashamed of his vision, and he will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive."

- **The hairy cloak as prophetic disguise.** The rough or hairy garment was the traditional dress of prophets, associated especially with Elijah (2 Kings 1:8) and John the Baptist (Matthew 3:4). False prophets wore it to deceive people into thinking they were genuine. In the coming day they will be too ashamed to don it. Gill adds that this points to monks and friars who "under the guise of sanctity and devotion, and of an austere and mortified life, impose their lies and deceptions" (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary:** They will no longer be permitted to "wear sackcloth or a rough garment, the badge of a prophet, to conceal their deceit" (Garner-Howes).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 5: "He will say, ‘I am not a prophet; I work the land, for I was purchased as a servant in my youth.’"

- **False prophets deny their former calling.** So great will be the shame that former false prophets will vigorously deny ever having been prophets. They will claim to be simple farmers or herdsmen — much like Amos, who genuinely was a herdsman (Amos 7:14) — to escape association with false prophecy. The BSB's "purchased as a servant in my youth" (or NKJV "man taught me to keep cattle from my youth") suggests they will claim a secular, agricultural upbringing.
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Gill** applies this to former Roman clergy who, after the fall of their system, will be forced to work for a living because "no man hereafter will buy of his merchandise" (cf. Revelation 18:11). They will deny ever having been clergy at all (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 6: "If someone asks him, ‘What are these wounds on your chest?’ he will answer, ‘These are the wounds I received in the house of my friends.’"

- **Wounds from pagan ecstatic practices.** It was common for false prophets (especially prophets of Baal) to cut or wound themselves in idolatrous rites (1 Kings 18:28; Jeremiah 48:37). When questioned about scars or wounds on the body (literally "between your hands/arms," meaning the chest or back), the accused false prophet offers a lame, evasive excuse — a brawl at a friend's house.
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Not a direct Messianic prophecy.** The KJV translates "wounds in thine hands," which has led some to apply this to Christ's nail scars. However, Guzik (following Calvin and Clarke) strongly rejects this: the Hebrew says "between your hands" (chest/body), and the context clearly concerns false prophets. Calvin called the Messianic application "very puerile," and Adam Clarke said he "cannot hear such an application of them without horror" (Enduring Word, quoting both).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Gill, however,** presents an alternative reading from Capellus: some understand these words as spoken by Christ — the Jews upbraid Him for His crucifixion wounds, and He replies that He was wounded by those of His own nation who "pretended to be the friends of the Messiah." But Gill himself treats this as an alternative, not his primary reading (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary** takes the minority view, applying v. 6 directly to Christ: "one shall inquire of Christ, the Messiah, 'What are these wounds or scars in thine hands?' … To which He shall respond, 'Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends'" (Garner-Howes).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 7: "Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd, against the man who is My Companion, declares the LORD of Hosts. Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn My hand against the little ones."

- **Jesus Himself quotes this verse.** In Matthew 26:31, just before Gethsemane, Jesus quotes "Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered" and applies it to His own impending arrest and the scattering of the disciples. This is the interpretive key to the whole verse (Guzik, JFB, Gill).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **God the Father commands the sword.** It is the LORD of Hosts Himself who calls, "Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd." This was not Satan's victory or a tragic accident; it was God's ordained, planned work. Guzik compares Isaiah 53:10: "Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise Him." God gave the command to strike the Shepherd (Enduring Word).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **"The man who is My Companion" points to Christ's deity.** The Hebrew word translated "Companion" (עָמִית, *amith*) is used in Leviticus for a "near neighbor." According to Keil (quoted by Guzik), this Shepherd "dwells side by side with the Lord, His equal" — one who "participates in the divine nature, or is essentially divine." JFB calls it "the man of my union" and notes the Hebrew for "man" here means "a mighty man" — "one peculiarly man in his noblest ideal." Hengstenberg glosses "My nearest kinsman," and De Wette (a Rationalist) concedes it means "My equal" (JFB).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **Gill:** "the man [that is] my fellow" describes Christ's human nature by "the man" and His divine nature by "the fellow of the Lord of hosts" — "not only being near to him in place and affection, but his equal, being truly a divine Person; of the same nature, glory, and majesty with him" (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **"I will turn My hand against the little ones."** JFB interprets "turn My hand upon" in a favorable sense (as in Isaiah 1:25 — refining). The "little ones" are the humble followers of Christ, the "poor of the flock" (Zechariah 11:7, 11). God's hand was laid in wrath on the Shepherd so that His hand might be turned in grace upon the little ones (JFB). Guzik notes that the BSB "against" may be misleading; the sense is God's hand of protection and restoration upon the small and humble remnant.
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **A Baptist dispensational reading** (Garner-Howes): This verse is a "prophetic call for the sword to be lifted against the Shepherd of the Lord, his fellow associate of the godhead." When the Shepherd was smitten, the sheep (the disciples, and Israel more broadly) were scattered. God then "pledged to turn His hand of help, or protection upon the little ones, the humble flock-followers of Him" — His church, whom He commissioned and comforted after the resurrection (Garner-Howes).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html

---

### v. 8: "And in all the land, declares the LORD, two-thirds will be cut off and perish, but a third will be left in it."

- **A future judgment on Israel.** The Pulpit Commentary says "in all the land" refers to Palestine, the country where the good Shepherd tended His flock (ch. 11), and which is a figure of the kingdom of God. Two-thirds perish; one-third survives (Pulpit, via search excerpt).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/zechariah/13.htm

- **Guzik** places this in the Great Tribulation context: "only one-third of the Jewish people will survive the great tribulation. If this is the case, no wonder these years are called the time of Jacob's trouble (Jeremiah 30:7)" (Enduring Word).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **JFB** notes that two-thirds of the Jewish nation were to perish "in the Roman wars, and a third to survive," but adds that the context (Zechariah 14:2–9) has "never yet been fulfilled" — so the destruction of two-thirds and saving of the remnant "are still future, and to be fulfilled under Antichrist" (JFB).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **Gill** applies this not to ethnic Jews alone but to the professing church worldwide: "two parts therein shall be cut off and die; all hypocrites, formalists, and outward court worshippers; who seem as if they would be at this time two thirds of the professors of true religion." He connects this to the last struggle of the beast of Rome (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Cambridge Bible:** The "third part" represents the faithful among the Jews (Romans 11:5) and the Christian Church gathered from all nations (cf. Isaiah 6:13; Ezekiel 5:2, 12) (Cambridge, via search excerpt).
  - https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/zechariah/13.htm

---

### v. 9: "This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold. They will call on My name, and I will answer them. I will say, ‘They are My people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is our God.’"

- **Refined, not destroyed.** The remnant is brought "through the fire" — the imagery is of a refiner's crucible, not a consuming fire. As silver and gold are purified by fire, so the faithful remnant is purified through tribulation. JFB cross-references Psalm 66:10, Amos 4:11, 1 Corinthians 3:15, and 1 Peter 1:6–7. He notes that Israel's conversion does not precede but follows their external deliverance (JFB).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **Covenant language.** The closing exchange — "They are My people" / "The LORD is our God" — is classic covenant formula (cf. Jeremiah 30:18–22; Ezekiel 11:19–20; Hosea 2:23). Guzik sees this as prophesying the Jewish remnant who survive the Great Tribulation and form the core of restored Israel under Messiah's millennial reign, including the 144,000 of Revelation 7 and 14 (Enduring Word).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

- **Pulpit Commentary:** This represents "God's dealing with his Church in every age." The third part, like its Master, "passes through much tribulation, and is thereby refined and purified." In their distress they turn in faith to Jehovah and He answers (Pulpit, via search excerpt).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/zechariah/13.htm

- **Gill,** applying this to the purified post-tribulation church, sees the refining fire as "the hour of temptation … in the Philadelphian church state" (Revelation 3:10) and the time of the slaying of the witnesses (Revelation 11:7). After refining, "a more pure and glorious state of the church will take place" (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Precept Austin** summarizes the whole arc: "They will call on My name, and I will answer them … This prophetically refers to the Jewish people who survive the great tribulation, come to salvation … and welcome Jesus in the name of the LORD." The fountain was opened at Calvary; Israel will finally enter into it (Precept Austin).
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/zechariah-13-commentary

## Tradition-Specific Readings

### Reformed / Presbyterian
- **JFB** (broadly Reformed) emphasizes divine sovereignty in v. 7: Christ's death was not man's triumph but God's act. "God regards sin in such a fearful light that He spared not His own co-equal Son." The sword is "judicial power," and its highest exercise is "to take away the life of the condemned." Yet God in this shows His love "as gloriously as His justice" — for God calls Messiah "My Shepherd," provided for sinners by His love (JFB).
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jfb/zechariah/13.htm

- **John Calvin** (quoted by Guzik) rejected applying v. 6 to Christ: "it is quite evident that he speaks here of false teachers, who had for a time falsely pretended God's name." He called the Messianic reading "very puerile" (Enduring Word, quoting Calvin).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

### Baptist
- **Charles Spurgeon** on v. 1: The fountain is inexhaustible, open, and accessible to all. "The means by which sin and sinfulness can be put away are at this moment accessible to the sons of men. The atonement is not a fountain hid and concealed, and closed and barred and bolted, it is a fountain open." He also sees a future fulfilment for ethnic Israel: "There will be a day when those who have so long refused to acknowledge Jesus as the Messias shall discern the marks of his mission" (Spurgeon).
  - https://www.spurgeon.org/sermons/the-open-fountain

- **John Gill** (Particular Baptist) on v. 2 reads the chapter through a historicist lens, identifying the idols as Roman Catholic images, the false prophet as the Pope, and the unclean spirit as the Jesuits, monks, and friars. He sees vv. 2–6 as fulfilled at the fall of mystical Babylon (Gill).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/zechariah-13.html

- **Garner-Howes Baptist Commentary** takes a dispensational, futurist approach: v. 6 uniquely applies to Christ's wounds, and vv. 8–9 refer to "the suffering of the remnant, preceding the final battle of Armageddon." Two-thirds perish at "the Antichrist's incited Armageddon against Israel" (Garner-Howes).
  - https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/zechariah-13.html

### Pentecostal / Charismatic
- **David Guzik** (Enduring Word) is broadly evangelical with charismatic leanings. He applies the chapter in a consistently futurist, premillennial framework: the fountain opens for ethnic Israel at the end of the Great Tribulation, and the surviving third forms the core of Israel in the millennial kingdom. However, he also applies the fountain devotionally to all believers now — it is "open and accessible, not hidden away" (Enduring Word).
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/zechariah-13/

### Anglican
- **Cambridge Bible for Schools and Colleges** (Anglican): On v. 1, "The form of the promise is Jewish, the substance Christian." On vv. 8–9, the "third part" includes both the Jewish remnant (Romans 11:5) and the Christian Church gathered from all nations. **Ellicott's Commentary** (Anglican) was referenced but could not be fetched in full due to tool limits.
  - https://www.biblehub.com/commentaries/cambridge/zechariah/13.htm

## Summary of Key Interpretive Differences

| Issue | Majority / Traditional View | Minority / Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **v. 6 wounds** | False prophets' self-inflicted wounds; not Messianic (Calvin, Clarke, Guzik) | Messianic: Christ's nail wounds (Garner-Howes Baptist; Capellus, noted by Gill) |
| **vv. 8–9 timing** | Future Great Tribulation (Guzik, JFB, Precept Austin) | Already partially fulfilled in AD 70, with final fulfilment still future (JFB); or refers to church-age purification (Gill, Pulpit) |
| **v. 2 false prophet** | Generic false prophets eliminated in the messianic age | Specifically the Papacy and Roman system (Gill — historicist Protestant) |
| **"My Companion" (v. 7)** | Points to Christ's equality with God — evidence of His deity (Keil, JFB, Gill, Guzik) | Some rabbinic interpreters applied this to a human king (Jarchi: king of Moab; other Jewish writers: king of Ishmael/Turkey — noted by Gill) |
